domain.description:
The subject area a record belongs to. A TAG SET, not a partition: a ledger record carries `domains[]` and may carry several, a series carries exactly one, and a phase is not a domain — phase 7 produced eight records filed across seven values.

THE DISTINCTION THAT GETS CONFUSED IS welfare AGAINST human-development: welfare is the DELIVERY of a scheme, human-development is the OUTCOME it was meant to produce. Records carrying both (Swachh Bharat, PM-JAY, the anaemia reversal) are the normal case, not an error — the scheme is one domain and what it did to people is another. Education holds both the delivery and the outcome of schooling; it is not split across welfare and human-development the way a scheme is.
- macro: aggregate economic conditions and fiscal or monetary policy.
- banking: banks, credit, financial supervision and resolution.
- employment: work, labour force, earnings and formality.
- poverty: measured deprivation and consumption-based poverty.
- human-development: outcomes in health, nutrition and survival — what delivery produced.
- infrastructure: physical networks and their capacity or service.
- welfare: scheme delivery and entitlements — what was provided.
- education: schooling and higher education — learning, participation, teaching capacity and the education system.
- governance: institutions of state, enforcement, transparency and rights.
- kashmir: a cross-cutting lens, applied to records whose primary subject sits elsewhere.
- federalism: Centre-state relations. Also a lens: GST and groundwater carry it alongside their own subject.
- foreign: trade, external balances and relations with other states.
- defence: armed conflict and counter-insurgency operations, external or internal. The state’s treatment of civilians in those operations files governance, not defence.
- environment: land, water, air and the resource base.

lenses.description:
A cross-cutting LENS the record is also read under. `domain` says what the record IS ABOUT; `lenses[]` says what it ALSO BEARS ON. They are two axes, and a single-valued `domain` cannot hold both — every phase-11 series is substantively a defence or governance measurement AND is about Jammu and Kashmir, and while only the first was expressible a reader filtering the instrument on `kashmir` reached no measured spine at all. Optional; absent means no lens applies, which is the ordinary case. A lens is never a substitute for the subject: the substantive subject always goes in `domain`.
- kashmir: Jammu and Kashmir as place and question — the record's subject sits elsewhere (defence, governance, welfare) and J&K is the territory, population or conflict it is measured over. NEVER a subject value. The domain enum's own line reads "a cross-cutting lens, applied to records whose primary subject sits elsewhere", so `domain: "kashmir"` declares a lens and no subject at all, and is an error (rule `lens-as-subject`).
- federalism: Centre-state relations bearing on a record whose subject is elsewhere — GST as a macro record that moves fiscal authority between Centre and states, groundwater as an environment record on a state subject. UNLIKE kashmir this value is ALSO a subject in its own right ("Centre-state relations"), so `domain: "federalism"` is legal. What is not legal is asserting it on both axes of one record: either alone is correct, both at once says the record's subject is a lens over itself (rule `lens-duplicated`).

SIX VALUES ADDED IN PHASE 14, AND THEY ARE A DIFFERENT SHAPE FROM THE FIRST TWO. `kashmir` and `federalism` were derived FROM the domain enum, which had written both as lenses; these six are not domain values and never will be. A counterparty is not a subject area — "china" answers WHO a record is about, not WHAT it is about, and the subject of every one of them is trade, external balances or relations, which is `foreign`. The lens axis is therefore wider than the subset-of-domains relation it happened to have while it held only two values, and `lenses[]` being a subset of the domain enum was an accident of its first population, not a rule.
A LENS IS ADMITTED WHEN ITS RECORDS LAND, NOT WHEN IT IS PLANNED. `china`, `neighbourhood` and `europe` are named in the phase-14 plan and are deliberately NOT in the enum above: they enter with the records that populate them. A declared value with nothing behind it is a filter that returns nothing to the reader who selects it, which is the same defect as a lens with no page one level in — and the `lens-empty` gate refuses the build rather than trusting an author to notice.
A COUNTERPARTY LENS IS DECLARED ONLY WHERE THE INSTRUMENT HOLDS A FILE — several records read together because the counterparty is itself the policy object. It is not declared for a single agreement: a lens over one record is a filter that returns what a reader already had. UAE CEPA and Australia ECTA carry no counterparty lens for that reason, and the vocabulary extends when a file forms, not when a country is mentioned.
- defence-sector: the record's subject is the armed forces, the defence industry or defence procurement, whatever domain it files. DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED `defence`, because the domain of that name is narrower — "armed conflict and counter-insurgency operations" — and the lens is wider than it: an acquisition cost files `macro`, an indigenisation share files `foreign`, and neither is armed conflict. Two names for two different extents, so neither can be read as the other.
- united-states: the United States as counterparty — tariff actions, the negotiation track, visa and services measures, defence and technology frameworks.
- china: the People's Republic as counterparty — the merchandise deficit and its composition, import dependence and export controls, investment screening, and post-Galwan normalisation READ AS A DIPLOMATIC INSTRUMENT. The conflict itself is phase 11's and files `defence`; this lens is not a route to restating it.
- russia: the Russian Federation as counterparty — crude and refined-product flows, payment mechanisms, defence supply, and the linkage of any of them into a third country's measures.
- neighbourhood: the immediate South Asian neighbourhood as ONE object, which is why it is one value and not seven. The counterparty lenses above are each a file because each state is individually a policy object; here the region is the stated policy object — "Neighbourhood First" names a region, not a country — and the records are read as a set. A reader wanting one country reads the titles, and if a single neighbour accumulates a file of its own it earns its own value then. Pakistan is a member of the region and the member the doctrine least describes; its records are not yet authored.
- europe: the EU, the UK and EFTA as counterparties. One value, because the three are one negotiating arc in this instrument's material — an in-force UK agreement, an in-force EFTA agreement carrying an investment commitment, and a live EU negotiation — and splitting them would give each a filter with one record behind it.

tier.description:
Evidence grade of the DOCUMENT ACTUALLY RETRIEVED, not of the institution the subject belongs to. This is the operative rule and the one that goes wrong: a CAG finding known only through a newspaper's account of an RTI reply is T4, because the subject is official but the evidence is relayed. Grade what you hold, not what it is about.
- T1: official Indian statistical or institutional source, retrieved directly - a ministry release, an RBI, MoSPI or NCRB publication, a CAG report, a Parliamentary reply.
- T1F: a NON-INDIAN NATIONAL GOVERNMENT primary, retrieved directly - a foreign executive order, statute, court judgment, trade-representative determination or official gazette. Added 2026-08-06 on operator ruling. T1 is Indian official and T2 is multilateral; a foreign national government is neither. A LETTER RATHER THAN A NUMBER, because the ladder's numbers descend in evidentiary strength and a foreign gazette is not weaker evidence than a contested composite index: T1F is T1's grade of artefact issued by a different state.
- T2: multilateral or international statistical source, retrieved directly - World Bank, IMF, ILO, WHO.
- T3: peer-reviewed research or a working paper.
- T4: reported or documentary journalism, NGO datasets, and anything RELAYED rather than retrieved - including an official figure known only through a press account, and an RTI reply cited but not obtained.
- T5: contested composite index. Always carries a dispute record covering its own domain (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
Note that tier is asserted in exactly one place per layer: on the series itself, or on each entry of a ledger or provenance `sources[]`. A series `source` is a SourceRef and carries NO tier - the object is closed, so a tier inside it is rejected rather than silently ignored.

vintage.description: Download/access date, to whatever precision the source states. Required for WDI and any source that revises history.

calendar.description: Indian fiscal year (Apr-Mar) or calendar year. Never mix within one series.

provenanceRef.description: Provenance record id (P-nn) documenting the change this break marks.

country.description:
Which country the OBSERVATION measures — not where the source sits. A WDI table published in Washington reporting Bangladesh carries BGD.
IND plus a fixed four-country peer panel, held constant so peer comparisons stay like-for-like (P-09 governs vintage discipline across the panel).
- IND: India, the subject of the instrument.
- BGD: Bangladesh · VNM: Vietnam · IDN: Indonesia · CHN: China — the comparator panel.
The `-peer` suffix on a series id is a naming convention, not a rule: gdp-per-capita-usd, lpi-rank, manufacturing-gdp and sanitation-basic carry panel points without it.

value.description: Null only with status "pending": the period is known to exist and no figure is yet held. A blank is unreported, never zero (CLAUDE.md rule 4).

status.description: verified = pinned to the named source this project cycle; approx = from a credible report, exact primary pull outstanding; pending = placeholder, must not render without a flag

items.description: Provenance record id (P-nn) whose measurement dispute bears on this series.

caveat.description: A blocking qualification that MUST render wherever this record appears, including compact listings. Use only when the record would mislead without it — an unverified comparability assumption, a circular measure, a disputed instrument. Not for ordinary uncertainty, which belongs in notes.

unmeasured.description: Dimensions this record SHOULD have but which have no measurement. An absence is a research finding, not an empty cell — declaring it here keeps it visible in every view rather than only where a component happens to supply it. Use when a chain has a missing link, an intended outcome was never measured, or a series stops short of the thing it is cited to demonstrate.

what.description: The thing that is not measured, stated positively

why.description: Why no figure exists — not collected, not published, withheld, or never defined

wouldFill.description: The source that would close it, if one is identifiable. Doubles as a verification-queue seed.

reasonKind.description:
The STATED reason no figure exists — what the responsible body says, not what is true. Where the stated reason is contradicted, set reasonDisputed and carry the contradiction in `why`.

THE TEST IS WHETHER THE DATA EXISTS, asked in this order:
- not-collected: never gathered. No record exists to release. If the holder were compelled tomorrow they would have nothing to produce.
- not-published: exists in a holder's hands, not released. The test is producibility under compulsion, not whether anyone has asked.
- withheld: exists, release was specifically requested or legally required, and was refused. Narrower than not-published — requires an identifiable refusal, not merely absence of release.
- never-defined: no agreed definition exists for the quantity, so it could not be collected even in principle. NOT "nobody has studied it" — an unstudied but definable quantity is not-collected.

reasonDisputed.description: True where the stated reason is contradicted by evidence — for example a body saying data was never maintained while another arm of the same government publishes some of it. The contradiction must be stated in `why`. This is not a fifth reasonKind: it is a dispute about which kind applies.

disputeKind.description:
What kind of contradiction reasonDisputed records. Required when reasonDisputed is true.
- evidentiary: the stated reason is contradicted by evidence that the data exists or was held.
- normative: the factual claim is not contested; what is contested is the characterisation of the non-release, typically against a legal or judicial obligation.

higherIsBetter.description: Direction of merit. true = higher is better, false = lower is better, NULL = the series has no agreed direction and must render with no directional cue at all. Null is a real value, not a missing one: a conviction rate and an enforcement count are read differently by different readers, and asserting a direction would take a side. RENDERED FROM 2026-08-12, discharging the debt this description carried. It is declared in tools/lib/value-renderings.mjs as a phrase over all three branches and renders through DirectionMark on every series page, because the question routes at /questions/ SELECT on it and a criterion a reader cannot check is not a criterion. WITHDRAWN WORDING, which this supersedes: the description said that “no view reads this field”, that lib/types.ts was “the only file in the repository that mentions it”, and that the exemption “records a DEBT, not a decision: the field is unimplemented rather than deliberately unrendered”. All three are now false. The exemption MARKER ITSELF is deliberately not reproduced in this quotation: it is a token two gates test for by substring, and a quotation containing it would silently re-exempt the field the moment anyone removed the declaration — the same shape as a correction guard that asserts an absence. The cue is WORDS AND NEVER COLOUR, and the null branch is the reason rather than the palette rule alone: a word can say “no agreed direction”, whereas a colour must choose a neutral shade, which reads as a third position on a scale instead of a refusal to take one. An ABSENT field renders nothing at all — 123 series have never been asked the question and 76 were asked and declined, and only the second is a declaration.

xAxis.description: What the period axis counts. Defaults to calendar-year. lok-sabha-term means each point is a Lok Sabha term identified by its first year, so the spacing is electoral rather than annual and the points must not be read as a yearly series. NOT A RENDERED VALUE: no view reads this field. Two series declare `lok-sabha-term` and both are rendered as an ordinary yearly series, which is what the sentence above forbids — so this is a LIVE RENDERING DEFECT on those two records and not merely an unrendered field. Exempted so the gate reports the debt rather than blocking every build on it; logged as an open item. Written 2026-08-06.

denominator.description: What the number is measured against, stated so it can render on the face of the value. A conviction rate of 0.25% and one of 93% can be the same enforcement record measured two ways (P-52), so a rate without its denominator is not a figure a reader can use. Null is a real value meaning the denominator is not yet established — it does not mean "not applicable", and the gate rejects it on a series that expresses a rate and carries P-52.
